nws.synopsis: Weak to moderate Santa Ana winds will continue through the weekend. High temperatures 5-15 degrees above normal for the coastal areas and valleys, warmest on Sunday. Winds weaken into next week as high pressure moves into the area, keeping temperatures above normal. A weather system may near the area by later next week, bringing cooler weather with a chance for rain.
systems: Current 500mb analysis plots an upper low swinging through northern Mexico this afternoon, with a ridge axis extending from central CA into the Great Basin.
This is providing northerly flow aloft, with the surface high placed in the Great Basin.
The offshore winds also look to have peaked compared to earlier this morning, but will still remain breezy into this afternoon.
Temperatures are quite mild as a result of the offshore flow, with many coastal/valley locations in the mid to upper 80s, about 10-15 degrees above seasonal averages.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. Launch in the light air before the switch; the west wind then builds the convergence inland (Perris, Hemet, Soboba). XC wants 7-8k over the range during the switch and the same or more inland.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Whale's V
sites.note: SW-facing bowl across Otay Lakes Rd from Skydive San Diego. Non-permitted, not a club site: coordinate with the DZ, never land at the DZ, no north wind at all. Ridge plus thermal site flying; a few hundred feet over launch is a good day, XC on great days. Under the SAN approach (3,500 ft), not part of the rating. Launch and LZ heights are estimates.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse / Fuzz
sites.note: Convergence sites: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert, Fuzz is flown on the same convergence. Horse and Laguna are scored on their own and the better one is shown. Horse can also have a glass-off in a light W-SW evening breeze; Laguna has none. The rating only says whether the setup is there; where and when the convergence sits, and the morning winds, are for you to check.

sites.name: Santa Barbara / Ojai
sites.note: Experimental trip area: the Santa Barbara front range (Skyport, EJ Bowl) and Ojai (Chief's Peak), with points along the crest between them. South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back. The range and a capping inversion near ridge height squeeze onshore S-SE flow (venturi: stronger and gustier at the ridgeline than the models show) but block a north wind aloft when the lapse rate is strong.

sites.name: Owens Valley
sites.note: Experimental trip area. Big-air site: the main launches are Walt's Point (Sierra side) and Paiute and Flynn's (White Mountains side). We look for high days (10,000 ft+) with almost no wind; any real wind sinks it. Advanced pilots only.
